content: Serotonin syndrome has been reported in patients treated with palonosetron, regardless of whether they have a known hypersensitivity to other 5-HT3 receptor antagonists. This condition has been observed more frequently when palonosetron is used in combination with serotonergic drugs, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), mirtazapine, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, or intravenous methylene blue. If symptoms of serotonin syndrome occur, discontinue the use of netupitant/palonosetron immediately. There is limited data available regarding the use of netupitant/palonosetron in pregnant women, and the information is insufficient to determine the risk of adverse developmental outcomes associated with the drug. Additionally, there is no data on the presence of netupitant (or fosnetupitant) or palonosetron in human breast milk, nor on their effects on breastfed infants or milk production. When considering the use of netupitant/palonosetron in breastfeeding mothers, weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother’s clinical need for the medication and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child or from the underlying maternal condition. Netupitant/palonosetron is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy when controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. However, it should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. The product does not contain antimicrobial preservatives and should be infused over 30 minutes. After the infusion, flush the infusion line with the same carrier solution to ensure complete drug administration. Netupitant/palonosetron capsules can be taken with or without food. Always read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you receive a refill. Headache is a possible side effect of this medication. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Palonosetron, one of the components of this product, may increase serotonin levels and, in rare cases, cause a serious condition known as serotonin syndrome or serotonin toxicity. The risk of serotonin syndrome increases if you are also taking other drugs that increase serotonin levels. Inform your doctor or pharmacist of all the medications you are taking to avoid potential drug interactions. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to netupitant, palonosetron, or other anti-nausea serotonin blockers (such as ondansetron), or if you have any other allergies. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this product passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of this product from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. Examples include rifamycins (such as rifampin) and St. John’s wort. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are also taking other drugs that increase serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs such as MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants, including SSRIs (such as fluoxetine and paroxetine) and SNRIs (such as duloxetine and venlafaxine). In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
